exam_set.title: Book 1 — Chapter 2 — Practice Set 3
exam_set.description: Textbook Practice — Book 1, Chapter 2, Practice Set 3

questions.jp: 後置記法（逆ポーランド記法）では，例えば，式Y＝(A－B)×CをYAB－C×＝と表現する。次の式を後置記法で表現したものはどれか。Y＝(A＋B)×(C－D÷E)
questions.romaji: Kochi kiho (gyaku Porando kiho) de wa, tatoeba, shiki Y = (A - B) × C o Y A B - C × = to hyogen suru. Tsugi no shiki o kochi kiho de hyogen shita mono wa dore ka. Y = (A + B) × (C - D ÷ E).
questions.en: In postfix notation (Reverse Polish notation), for example, Y=(A-B)×C is written as Y A B - C × =. Which postfix expression represents Y=(A+B)×(C-D÷E)?

options.label: ア
options.romaji: Y A B + C - D E ÷ × =
options.en: Y A B + C - D E ÷ × =

options.label: イ
options.romaji: Y A B + C D E ÷ - × =
options.en: Y A B + C D E ÷ - × =

options.label: ウ
options.romaji: Y A B + E D C ÷ - × =
options.en: Y A B + E D C ÷ - × =

options.label: エ
options.romaji: Y B A + C D E ÷ - × =
options.en: Y B A + C D E ÷ - × =

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Postfix notation writes the numbers or letters first and puts each operator after the values it uses. Convert the small parenthesized parts before joining them.

Technical breakdown:
Convert (A+B):

A B +

Convert D÷E:

D E ÷

Then convert (C-D÷E):

C D E ÷ -

Multiply the two completed parts:

A B + C D E ÷ - ×

Following the source's assignment convention, add Y at the front and = at the end:

Y A B + C D E ÷ - × =

Japanese keywords to remember:
後置記法 = kochi kiho = postfix notation
逆ポーランド記法 = gyaku Porando kiho = Reverse Polish notation
演算子 = enzanshi = operator
演算対象 = enzan taisho = operand
表現する = hyogen suru = to represent
式変換 = shiki henkan = expression conversion

Why the best solution works:
Option イ preserves operand order and places ÷ after D and E, - after C and the division result, and × after the two parenthesized results.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア — It places subtraction before the D÷E subexpression has been formed, so the original precedence and grouping are lost.

ウ — It reverses the operands involved in the division/subtraction region; subtraction and division are not commutative.

エ — It reverses A and B relative to the source expression. Even though addition happens to be commutative, it is not a faithful postfix conversion of the written operand order.

Memory trick:
Normal: A + B. Postfix: A B +. The operator goes after its operands.

Correct answer: イ

questions.jp: 表は，文字列を検査するための状態遷移表である。検査では，初期状態をaとし，文字列の検査中に状態がeになれば不合格とする。解答群で示される文字列のうち，不合格となるものはどれか。ここで，文字列は左端から検査し，解答群中の△は空白を表す。
questions.romaji: Hyo wa, mojiretsu o kensa suru tame no jotai sen'i-hyo de aru. Kensa de wa, shoki jotai o a to shi, mojiretsu no kensachu ni jotai ga e ni nareba fugokaku to suru. Kaito-gun de shimesareru mojiretsu no uchi, fugokaku to naru mono wa dore ka. Koko de, mojiretsu wa satan kara kensa shi, kaito-gunchu no sankaku wa kuhaku o arawasu.
questions.en: The table is a state-transition table for checking strings. The initial state is a, and a string fails if state e is reached while it is checked. Which answer string fails? Strings are checked from the left, and the triangle symbol represents a blank space.
questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Do not decide whether a string looks like a number. Start at a and use the table once for every character. If the path ever reaches e, the string fails.

Technical breakdown:
For 12.2, begin at a:

1 (digit): a → b
2 (digit): b → b
. (decimal point): b → d
2 (digit): d → e

State e is reached, so 12.2 is invalid. The other choices can be traced without entering e: +0010 follows the permitted sign-and-digit path, -1 follows the permitted sign-and-digit path, and 9△ follows the permitted digit-and-blank path. The triangle is a blank, not a literal triangle character.

Japanese keywords to remember:
状態遷移表 = jotai sen'i-hyo = state-transition table
初期状態 = shoki jotai = initial state
文字列 = mojiretsu = string
検査 = kensa = check
不合格 = fugokaku = invalid / fail
空白 = kuhaku = blank
数字 = suji = digit
符号 = fugo = sign
小数点 = shosuten = decimal point
現在の状態 = genzai no jotai = current state

Why the best solution works:
Option ウ reaches e on its final digit: d with a digit transitions to e. The rule says reaching e at any point makes the string fail.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア — Tracing the plus sign and following digits stays on valid transitions and never reaches e.

イ — The minus sign followed by a digit follows the valid sign path and does not enter e.

エ — Starting with 9 reaches the digit state, and the trailing blank follows the table's valid blank transition.

Memory trick:
Follow the state table one character at a time; never judge from what looks like a valid number.

Correct answer: ウ

questions.jp: 次の状態遷移図で表現されるオートマトンで受理されるビット列はどれか。ここで，ビット列は左から順に読み込まれるものとする。
questions.romaji: Tsugi no jotai sen'i-zu de hyogen sareru otomaton de juri sareru bitto-retsu wa dore ka. Koko de, bitto-retsu wa hidari kara jun ni yomikomareru mono to suru.
questions.en: Which bit string is accepted by the automaton represented by the following state-transition diagram? The bit string is read from left to right.
questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Trace each bit along an arrow. The accepting state is the double circle. The machine reaches it after moving to the middle on 1 and then reading 0.

Technical breakdown:
At the start state, 0 loops at the start and 1 moves to the middle. At the middle state, 1 loops there and 0 moves to the accepting state. At the accepting state, either 0 or 1 loops and remains accepted.

Trace 1010:

1 → middle
0 → accepting
1 → remain accepting
0 → remain accepting

Therefore 1010 is accepted. In general, after any leading zeros, the string must contain one or more 1s followed by a 0; later bits cannot undo acceptance.

Japanese keywords to remember:
状態遷移図 = jotai sen'i-zu = state-transition diagram
オートマトン = otomaton = automaton
受理 = juri = acceptance
ビット列 = bitto-retsu = bit string
読み込む = yomikomu = to read
初期状態 = shoki jotai = initial state
受理状態 = juri jotai = accepting state

Why the best solution works:
Option ウ contains the transition 1 then 0, reaches the double-circle state on its second bit, and stays accepted for the remaining bits.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア — Every 0 loops at the start, so the accepting state is never reached.

イ — The leading 0 stays at the start, then 1 reaches the middle; the remaining 1s loop there, with no 0 to reach acceptance.

エ — The first 1 reaches the middle and all later 1s stay there, so it is rejected.

Memory trick:
Trace arrows. Never judge acceptance from the bit pattern by intuition.

Correct answer: ウ
